findings.reader: A well-bounded, well-crafted dated news piece: it explains the September 16 OpenAI disclosure and the upload incident with its causal chain, explicitly refuses to generalize to all products or to a frequency claim, and converts the answer-versus-action distinction into three concrete permission questions at a recognizable handoff. Terms are defined in context, the single analogy maps accurately with limits retained, uncertainty survives to the ending, and the mechanism supports both explain-back and transfer to an unseen scenario.
findings.facts: Factually sound: the framework/six-reports claim, the upload example, the not-a-frequency-estimate caveat and the work-in-progress/internal-voluntary limits are each directly verifiable in the supplied OpenAI disclosure and AP report, with attribution and scope preserved. Dates are checkable, the AP analyst quote is characterized accurately, and the article never converts OpenAI's bounded self-disclosure into an industry-wide or product-level claim.
